summary: Ambient: 60-80 BPM or no felt pulse, long held chords on slow-attack pads, a low sub drone, sparse bells or piano, a barely-there soft pulse or no drums, long reverb and echo; knowledge/style/ambient.json is its template
body: Tempo: pure ambient has no felt tempo (events sparse and irregular); with a pulse, slow: 60-90 BPM (illbient mid-80s, ambient house low 120s).
Drums: none or a barely-there pulse: soft, dry or lightly reverbed, low-passed and far back (a CR-78's light kick, woodblock and hats); moving toward ambient, thin out and fade the drums first.
Bass: a sub drone rather than a bassline: long low held notes, warm and round, low-passed, its harmonics brought out slowly.
Harmony: single chords held for bars (2-8 bars each), major 7ths, sus and add9 chords, I-IV, I-vi, i-VI; pads with slow attack and release that swell and fade into each other.
Lead: little melody: a few sparse bell, celeste, kalimba or soft piano notes with long echoes; never a pad or wash as the lead.

Texture/master: spacious and soft: long hall reverbs and delays, wide stereo, field recordings or filtered noise optional, slow automation instead of section changes; no hard compression, no distortion.

Sources (2026-11-26): Mode Audio 'Ambient: 5 Production Essentials'; MusicRadar '26 inspirational and practical ambient music production tips'; EDMProd 'How to Make Ambient Music in 7 Easy Steps'; LANDR 'How to Make Ambient Music'.
Apply: pattern/prog-ambient-characteristic-3 on the keys. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/ambient.json instead.

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
